The base healing of this power is determined by rolling a number of d6 dice equal to half the user's SENSITIVITY modifier (e.g., if your character has a SENSITIVITY of 6, you would roll 3d6). {{user}} is PROHIBITED from using it more than once a day.

entries.name: Cryokinesis
entries.content:
Requires SEN 6; NVL 9.
With this power, experienced Jedi or Sith can manipulate the surrounding temperature to freeze objects or opponents in an area. This can cause significant damage (2d6 + SEN) or immobilize enemies for a short period of time. Success is determined by a SENSITIVITY test against the target's DC (10 + FOR of the target).

entries.name: Convection
entries.content:
Requires SEN 6; NVL 9.
Users can increase control over heat generation, creating an aura of intense heat that radiates around themselves or others. This heat provides elemental resistance or serves as a means to inflict fire-based damage to nearby enemies (1d8 + SEN) determined by a successful SENSITIVITY test against the target's DC (8 + target's FOR).

entries.name: Force Drain
entries.content:
Requires FOR 5, SEN 9; NVL 9.
Skilled Force practitioners can siphon an enemy's life energy, dealing damage (1d8 + user's SEN modifier) while healing themselves by the same amount. This powerful ability requires concentration, and success is determined by comparing the user's SENSITIVITY test to the opponent's relevant DC (10 + target's SEN).

entries.name: Force Reflection
entries.content:
Requires AGI 6, Lightsaber Deflection; NVL 9.
After extensive training with a lightsaber and honing your agility, you have mastered the ability to deflect incoming ranged attacks toward your enemies. Upon successfully deflecting a ranged attack using Lightsaber Deflection, you can now attempt to redirect the attack to an enemy of your choice within range as a swift action. To determine if you successfully hit the target enemy, make an additional ranged attack roll (d20 + AGI) against their defense.

entries.name: Advanced Mind Trick
entries.content:
Requires CAR 5; SEN 5; NVL 9; Medium Mind Trick.
This power grants total control over weak-minded people and allows users to control their actions for a long time. Enemies must pass a DC of 10 + the user's SENSITIVITY test to resist it. Only this version of the power works on Jedi/Sith.

entries.name: Onderon
entries.content: Onderon, a fierce Outer Rim planet, is known for dense jungles and the fortified city of Iziz. Its skies are turbulent, mirroring the struggle between civilization and wild nature. Nights bring predatory beasts like the massive, flying drexls, which jungle clans ride in battle. Onderon’s culture is warlike, with ongoing clashes between Iziz’s inhabitants and jungle tribes. Technology is sparse outside Iziz, and political power struggles have scarred its history, keeping tension alive across the planet.

entries.name: Vergesso Asteroids
entries.content: The Vergesso Asteroids are a chaotic asteroid field in the galaxy’s Outer Rim. Known for their treacherous navigation hazards, these asteroids are packed with dense metals and valuable minerals, making them a hot spot for mining and smuggling operations. Hidden deep within are secret bases and makeshift stations where outlaws, mercenaries, and the occasional Rebel operative set up shop, evading Imperial surveillance. The asteroid field's erratic movement and complex paths make it a perfect hideout but a dangerous place to operate. This area has become legendary for those seeking a discreet base, but only the most skilled or desperate dare venture into its depths.

entries.name: Taris
entries.content: Taris, once a prosperous city-planet, is now a haunting shadow of its former self, plagued by decay and ruin. Its towering skyscrapers and industrialized landscape once mirrored Coruscant, but centuries of warfare and a devastating Sith bombardment left it scarred and largely abandoned. Now, the surface is divided into layers: the wealthy inhabit the Upper City’s remnants, while the impoverished and criminal elements struggle to survive in the underworld of the Lower City and sewers. Mutant creatures known as rakghouls—victims of a terrifying plague—lurk in the depths, infecting and hunting the desperate survivors. Though Taris remains a grim, dangerous place, scavengers and explorers are drawn by rumors of ancient artifacts and valuable tech buried in its ruins.

entries.name: Kashyyyk
entries.content: Kashyyyk, the lush and towering homeworld of the Wookiees, is a planet of giant trees that stretch hundreds of meters into the sky, forming natural cities among the dense canopy. The Wookiees live in elevated tree cities, connected by bridges and platforms, with each level of the forest, called a "wroshyr tree tier," hosting different flora and fauna. While the upper levels are relatively safe, the lower depths, known as the Shadowlands, are dark and perilous, filled with dangerous creatures and untamed wilderness. During the Galactic Empire’s rise, Kashyyyk was subjected to brutal occupation, with many Wookiees enslaved or forced into hard labor. Despite this, the Wookiees remain fiercely loyal to each other and deeply connected to their ancestral lands, guarding their world with honor and unmatched streng

entries.name: Carida
entries.content: Carida, a rugged Core World, is famous for its harsh terrain and renowned Imperial Academy, which rigorously trains stormtroopers and officers. Its high gravity and severe climate make it ideal for conditioning recruits under extreme conditions. The academy features advanced facilities and combat simulators, shaping elite Imperial soldiers. Carida’s population is largely Imperial, giving it a strong military atmosphere, and its graduates are known across the galaxy for their discipline and strength.

entries.name: Nar Shadazzle
entries.content:
Also known as the "Smuggler's Moon," orbiting Nal Hutta and covered in urban sprawl.

Importance: A hub for criminal activities, controlled by the Hutts and filled with pirates, bounty hunters, and smugglers.

entries.name: Mandalore
entries.content:
Harsh, warlike planet, home to the Mandalorians. Characterized by deserts and rocky terrain.

Importance: Seat of a warrior culture known for being disciplined mercenaries and enemies of the Republic and Empire.

entries.name: Thyferra
entries.content:
Tropical world central to the production of bacta, a vital medicinal substance.

Importance: Controlled by the bacta cartel, making it key to the galactic economy and health.

entries.name: Dagobah
entries.content:
Swampy, dense jungle world hidden on the galaxy’s fringes.

Importance: Strong in the Dark Force.

entries.name: Endor
entries.content: Forest world inhabited by Ewoks, covered in dense vegetation and huge trees.

entries.name: Mygeeto
entries.content:
Frozen world with rare crystals, used in lightsaber construction.

Importance: Battleground during the Clone Wars, where Jedi fought against the Separatists.

entries.name: Mustafar
entries.content: Volcanic planet and site of Darth Vader’s fortress.

entries.name: Scarif
entries.content: Tropical world with beaches and lagoons, heavily fortified by the Empire.

entries.name: Muunilinst
entries.content:
World controlled by the Muuns, a species that manages the InterGalactic Banking Clan.

Importance: Financial center of the galaxy

entries.name: Geonosis
entries.content:
Desert world and home to the Geonosians, known for their hive-like factories.

Importance: Site of the first battle of the Clone Wars and the Separatist droid foundries.

entries.name: Ryloth
entries.content:
Arid planet, home to the Twi'leks. Alternates between extreme heat and freezing cold.

Importance: Known for constant invasions and the Twi'leks' resistance against slavery and occupation.

entries.name: Ziost
entries.content:
A frozen, dark Sith planet in the Outer Rim, with sinister energy tied to the Dark Side.

Importance: Former Sith stronghold and home to spirits of Dark Lords.

entries.name: Byss
entries.content:
Dark, hidden world in the Deep Core, where spirit of the Emperor Palpatine took refuge after his apparent death.

Importance: Center of Palpatine's cloning experiments and his possible return.

entries.name: Honoghr
entries.content:
Planet devastated and polluted by war. Home of the Noghri, who served as the Emperor's assassins.

Importance: Base of loyalty to Darth Vader,

entries.name: Tython
entries.content:
Mystical and spiritual world in the Deep Core, regarded as the birthplace of the Jedi Order.

Importance: Spiritual center for the Jedi in ancient times, where the Force was first explored.

entries.name: X-wing Starfighter (T-65)
entries.content:
Role: Versatile frontline starfighter in dogfights and space battles, and key in the assault on the Death Star.

Description: The X-wing is the backbone of the Rebel starfighter fleet. Known for its balance of speed, firepower, and durability, it’s equipped with four laser cannons and proton torpedo launchers.

Notable Missions: Destruction of both Death Stars and multiple battles throughout the Galactic Civil War.

entries.name: Y-wing Starfighter (BTL-A4 and BTL-S3)
entries.content:
Role: Primary bomber in the Rebel fleet, used in bombing runs and disabling enemy systems.

Description: Slower but heavily armored, the Y-wing carries ion cannons, laser turrets, and proton bombs, making it ideal for bombing runs against large targets.

Notable Missions: Y-wings led bombing runs on capital ships and Imperial facilities, especially in the Battle of Yavin.

entries.name: A-wing Interceptor (RZ-1)
entries.content:
Role: Designed to counter TIE fighters and disrupt Imperial formations with its superior speed.

Description: Known for its speed and agility, the A-wing was designed to counter Imperial TIE Interceptors. It carries two laser cannons and concussion missile launchers.

Notable Missions: Used in the Battle of Endor to engage fast-moving Imperial fighters.

entries.name: B-wing Starfighter (A/SF-01)
entries.content:
Description: Heavy starfighter armed with ion cannons, proton torpedoes, and laser cannons, designed to take down large ships.

Role: Anti-capital ship unit; its unique gyro-stabilized cockpit allows high maneuverability during assaults.

entries.name: Corellian Corvette (CR90)
entries.content:
Description: Light capital ship used for escort missions and quick, agile engagements. Famous for its modular design and adaptability.

Role: Transport, blockade runner, and command ship for smaller Rebel cells.

entries.name: Mon Calamari Star Cruiser (MC80)
entries.content:
Description: Main battleship of the Rebel fleet, equipped with turbolasers, ion cannons, and powerful shields.

Role: Heavy capital ship capable of taking on Imperial Star Destroyers in large fleet engagements.

entries.name: Mon Calamari Star Cruiser (MC80): "Independence"
entries.content:
Description: Main battleship of the Rebel fleet, equipped with turbolasers, ion cannons, and powerful shields.

Role: Heavy capital ship capable of taking on Imperial Star Destroyers in large fleet engagements.

Captain of this battleship: Admiral Ackbar.

entries.name: Nebulon-B Frigate
entries.content:
Description: Originally an Imperial escort vessel, the Nebulon-B was often used by the Rebellion for medical and escort roles.

Role: Medical frigate and support ship for Rebel fleets, such as the Redemption.

entries.name: GR-75 Medium Transport
entries.content:
Description: Non-combat transport ship used to move supplies, equipment, and troops.

Role: Primary logistics and troop transport vessel for evacuations and supply missions.

entries.name: Assault Frigate Mark I
entries.content:
Description: Modified Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser with improved speed, armor, and weaponry.

Role: Long-range support and assault operations, effective in large-scale battles.

entries.name: Quasar Fire-class Carrier
entries.content:
Description: Light carrier capable of deploying multiple starfighter squadrons.

Role: Carrier support for starfighter wings, used to launch fighters quickly into battle.

entries.name: Rebel Troopers
entries.content:
Description: Standard infantry with blaster rifles, often outfitted with guerrilla-style armor and camouflage.

Role: Core infantry force for holding positions, hit-and-run tactics, and ambushing Imperial forces.

entries.name: Pathfinders
entries.content:
Description: Elite Rebel commandos trained for reconnaissance and high-risk operations.

Role: Special forces unit used for sabotage, infiltration, and demolitions in high-priority missions.

entries.name: Rebel Heavy Weapons Team
entries.content:
Description: Infantry teams armed with heavy blasters, ion cannons, or missile launchers.

Role: Anti-vehicle and anti-air support for Rebel ground operations.

entries.name: SpecForce Infiltrators
entries.content:
Description: Highly trained infiltration rebel unit skilled in espionage, sabotage, and assassination.

Role: Covert operations deep within enemy lines, particularly for intelligence and sabotage missions.

entries.name: 1.4 FD P-Tower Anti-Infantry Laser Cannon
entries.content:
Description: Stationary laser cannon designed for anti-infantry and light vehicle support.

Role: Defensive emplacements, used to protect Rebel bases and outposts.

entries.name: DF.9 Anti-Infantry Battery
entries.content:
Description: Anti-personnel turret with a rapid-fire laser cannon for crowd control.

Role: Stationed at Rebel bases for defensive purposes against infantry assaults.

entries.name: T-2B Repulsorlift Tank
entries.content:
Description: Light armored vehicle with laser cannons, highly mobile and effective against Imperial armor.

Role: Primary Rebel armored unit, used for hit-and-run tactics against heavier Imperial vehicles.

entries.name: T-47 Airspeeder (Snowspeeder)
entries.content:
Description: Originally a civilian craft, modified with blasters and a tow cable for combat.

Role: Used extensively on Hoth for anti-vehicle combat, particularly effective against AT-ATs.

entries.name: Gallofree Medium Transport (GR-75)
entries.content:
Description: Same model as the space transport, repurposed for ground supply missions.

Role: Ground logistics, carrying supplies, troops, and vehicles for Rebel bases.

entries.name: AT-PT (All Terrain Personal Transport)
entries.content:
Description: Small, two-legged walker with light armor, offering a single pilot protection in rough terrain.

Role: Scout vehicle, used for reconnaissance and light fire support in difficult terrain.

entries.name: Z-95 Headhunter
entries.content:
Description: An older model starfighter with a single pair of wings, making it simpler in design compared to the X-wing. Known for its versatility, the Z-95 is fast and rugged, though less advanced. It typically has a green or gray paint scheme, depending on the squadron or faction using it.

Armament: Equipped with twin laser cannons, and some models carry concussion missiles. It lacks the proton torpedoes and hyperdrive of the X-wing but is highly adaptable for shorter missions.

Role: Often used by Rebel cells, planetary defense forces, and mercenary groups. While not as sophisticated as the X-wing, the Z-95 remains effective in skirmishes, providing solid firepower and maneuverability.
Importance: Its reliability made it popular among Rebel forces and Outer Rim defenders, giving it a legendary reputation as a “workhorse” fighter.

entries.name: Imdaar
entries.content:
Description: Imdaar is a remote and relatively obscure planet located in the Outer Rim Territories. It isn't widely known across the galaxy and has no significant population or bustling trade routes. The landscape is generally mysterious, as much of the planet remains uncharted and unexplored.

Significance: Imdaar becomes notable mainly due to its strategic importance for hidden Imperial operations. Imdaar was the site of secret Imperial research, including advanced fighter prototypes like the TIE Phantom, which could utilize cloaking technology. Imdaar's isolation and lack of attention made it ideal for secret military projects and experimental weapon development by the Empire.

entries.name: Kessel
entries.content:
Description: Kessel is a desolate, rocky planet known for its harsh, toxic environment and the infamous Kessel spice mines. The atmosphere is barely breathable, and much of the planet is covered in barren deserts and dangerous terrain. The high value of spice, specifically the addictive Glitterstim variety, made Kessel a hotbed for criminal activity and smuggling.

Significance: Kessel is most notorious for its slave-operated spice mines, controlled at different times by the Empire, various crime syndicates, and even Hutt cartels. Prisoners, enslaved workers, and political detainees were often sent to labor here in brutal conditions. Additionally, Kessel orbits near the Maw—a cluster of black holes that made navigation perilous but also provided a hidden route for smugglers who risked the "Kessel Run" to evade Imperial patrols.

Appearances: Kessel is featured in numerous Star Wars stories as a lawless, perilous location, famous for Han Solo's legendary Kessel Run.

entries.name: The Maw
entries.content:
Description: The Maw is a deadly region of space located near the Kessel sector, composed of a cluster of black holes tightly packed together. This dense gravitational anomaly creates extreme conditions, making it nearly impossible for most ships to navigate safely without precise charts. The Maw's gravitational pull is so intense that it distorts time and space, forming a twisted, nearly impassable maze of black holes, each in a precarious gravitational balance with the others.

Significance: The Maw's natural defenses and isolation made it the ideal hiding place for secret Imperial projects. The Empire, under the direction of Grand Moff Tarkin, established the Maw Installation—a top-secret research facility hidden within the black holes. Scientists at the Maw Installation were responsible for developing some of the galaxy’s most destructive weapons, including the original Death Star superlaser and the Sun Crusher, a starship capable of triggering supernovae.

Strategic Use: The Maw also played a significant role in smuggling operations, as experienced smugglers, like Han Solo, used the dangerous Kessel Run—a hyperspace route that skirts the edge of the Maw. Completing the Kessel Run in the shortest distance required perilous navigation near the black holes, allowing smugglers to evade Imperial detection.

entries.name: Abregado Rae
entries.content:
Description: Abregado Rae is a rugged, industrial planet located in the Mid Rim of the galaxy, known for its mining operations and factories. The planet’s surface is dotted with vast mining pits, processing plants, and shipyards. Its cities are built near the industrial zones, making the planet highly urbanized and somewhat polluted. The planet has an inhospitable climate, with desert-like terrain and harsh weather conditions that make it an unappealing place for most settlers, but its resources have made it strategically important.

Significance: Abregado Rae became known for its role as a major trade hub and port for the Imperial and Rebel factions during the Galactic Civil War. Due to its proximity to important hyperspace routes, it was a key location for shipping and logistics. Both the Empire and Rebel Alliance used the planet for clandestine operations. It was also home to several shipyards that produced starfighters and other military vehicles, making it a prime target for both sides.

Rebel Presence: Abregado Rae is notable for being a site of Rebel activity. Rebel forces operated from Abregado Rae in order to disrupt Imperial operations and make use of its strategic position. It was one of the many systems where the Rebels had a presence, conducting sabotage operations, smuggling, and guerrilla warfare.

entries.name: Mon Mothma
entries.content:
Role: Rebel Leader, Senator

Importance: Mon Mothma is the political leader of the Rebel Alliance and a symbol of hope and unity against the tyranny of the Empire. She is central in organizing the Rebellion's strategy and maintaining its alliances. She is a key figure in the Rebellion's leadership, ensuring the continuity of its cause despite overwhelming odds.

entries.name: Lando Calrissian
entries.content:
Role: Former Smuggler, Rebel Ally
Importance: Although not yet a formal member of the Rebel Alliance during the period between Yavin and Hoth wars, Lando Calrissian becomes an important ally and resource for the Rebels. His knowledge of the Outer Rim and his connections in the criminal underworld make him an asset to the Rebel cause, though he does not yet join in the fight against the Empire in full force during this timeframe.

entries.name: General Jan Dodonna
entries.content:
Role: Rebel General
Importance: A seasoned military leader, General Dodonna plays a pivotal role in the planning of the Battle of Yavin, providing valuable strategic advice and coordinating the Rebel defense. While not as prominent in the Battle of Hoth, his experience remains vital to Rebel leadership during this time period.

entries.name: Admiral Ackbar
entries.content:
Role: Rebel Admiral
Importance: Ackbar, a Mon Calamari military leader, begins his rise in the Rebel Navy during this period. He is a skilled tactician and strategist who leads Rebel forces during the planning and execution of various battles. By the time of the Battle of Hoth, Ackbar is a prominent leader, and his contributions to Rebel tactics would grow in importance later in the war.

entries.name: Wedge Antilles
entries.content:
Role: Rebel Pilot
Importance: Wedge is one of the most skilled pilots in the Rebel fleet and a key member of Red Squadron during the Battle of Yavin. He survives the attack on the Death Star and plays a crucial role in the Rebel Alliance’s efforts throughout the Galactic Civil War. Wedge is often seen leading or assisting in major space battles, including the defense of Hoth.

entries.name: R2-D2
entries.content:
Role: Astromech Droid
Importance: R2-D2 is crucial to the Rebel cause, particularly in his role as a starfighter astromech and an information carrier. R2 stores important data, including the Death Star plans, and plays a vital role in the communication systems of Rebel forces. His abilities as an astromech droid make him invaluable to both the pilots and leaders of the Rebellion.

entries.name: C-3PO
entries.content:
Role: Protocol Droid
Importance: Though not a fighter, C-3PO plays a key support role for the Rebel Alliance as a translator, diplomat, and information gatherer. He accompanies Leia, Han, and Luke on many missions and provides assistance during the critical moments of the Rebellion’s operations. He also plays a role in facilitating communication between the various Rebel factions.

entries.name: Chewbacca
entries.content:
Role: Wookiee Warrior, Rebel Pilot
Importance: Chewbacca is Han Solo’s loyal companion and co-pilot. As a skilled warrior and pilot, he plays an important role in several missions of the Rebel Alliance. His strength, loyalty, and combat abilities make him invaluable to the Rebellion, particularly during the escape from Yavin and the defense of Hoth.

entries.name: Han Solo
entries.content:
Role: Smuggler, Rebel Pilot
Importance: Han Solo, after aiding in the destruction of the Death Star, becomes an integral part of the Rebellion. Although initially motivated by money and a desire to stay out of political conflicts, Han grows to become a committed ally of the Rebel Alliance. He is involved in key missions leading up to the Battle of Hoth, where his leadership and piloting skills are vital.

entries.name: Princess Leia Organa
entries.content:
Role: Princess of Alderaan, Rebel Leader
Importance: Leia is a crucial leader in the Rebel Alliance, serving as a diplomat, strategist, and one of the foremost political figures in the fight against the Empire. She is also one of the survivors of Alderaan’s destruction and is a key player in the events surrounding the Battle of Yavin. During the period between Yavin and Hoth, she continues to be a vital leader and one of the most trusted members of the Rebellion.

entries.name: Luke Skywalker
entries.content:
Role: Jedi Knight, Rebel Pilot
Importance: Luke is one of the central heroes of the Rebellion, responsible for delivering the fatal blow to the first Death Star during the Battle of Yavin. After Yavin, he begins his training as a Jedi under Obi-Wan Kenobi and Yoda. By the time of the Battle of Hoth, Luke is fully committed to the fight against the Empire and is becoming a key figure in the Rebellion.
